ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: From a Kid to a Champion

fullPassage:
My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the breeze in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was held in our small town. I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your autograph?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was waiting at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!"

Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and insignificant. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before. Gabriel was from Bogotá, Colombia, which is high up in the Andes. He had a lot of experience in riding on hills and mountains, so he was always the first to arrive at the top. He would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic. Never stop pedaling, kid."

Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally paid off in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, who supports the leader and the team during a cycling race, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. All four of us fell in the crash, and the other teams passed us by. I was just slightly wounded, but Gabriel's injury was more serious. He urged me to continue on his behalf. But there were a couple of more steep slopes ahead, and I doubted we had a chance. Gabriel read my mind and yelled, "Remember the view at the top. Never stop pedaling whatever it takes, kid. Now go!"

Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!"

For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results flourished. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and insisted that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.

Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without hesitation, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits. When there were only 10 km left in the race, Gabriel caught up with us on a new bicycle. He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line."

Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors by a nose.

The crowd roared tremendously. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes.

He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes, saying, "We're counting on you, Captain."

questions.passage: My name is Bliksem, which means "lightning." My parents named me this because they wanted me to be faster than anyone else. Born in the Netherlands, a country with more bicycles than people, I learned to ride a bike almost as soon as I could walk. I loved feeling the (A)[breeze / storm] in my hair. When I was eleven, a junior bicycle race was (B)[held / canceled] in our small town. I entered the race as the (C)[youngest / oldest] rider.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 머리카락 사이로 부는 산들바람(breeze). 경주가 열렸다(held). 가장 어린(youngest) 선수로 참가.
det.analysis:
✅ ② breeze — held — youngest: 원문 일치.
❌ ① storm(폭풍): 자전거 타며 느끼는 감정과 어울리지 않음.
❌ ③ canceled(취소된): 참가했으므로 취소 아님.
❌ ④ oldest(가장 나이 많은): youngest의 반의어.
det.tip: breeze(산들바람) ↔ storm(폭풍), held(개최된) ↔ canceled(취소된).

questions.passage: As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You outran the others by two laps! You're a real racer, kid!" Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and (A)[passionate / indifferent] cyclists came together. I felt small and (B)[insignificant / important]. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell (C)[behind / ahead] in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 열정적인(passionate) 선수들만 모인 팀. 하찮게(insignificant) 느꼈다. 산악 경주에서 항상 뒤처졌다(behind).
det.analysis:
✅ ① passionate — insignificant — behind: 원문 일치.
❌ ② indifferent(무관심한): 프로팀은 열정적인 선수들의 모임.
❌ ③ important(중요한): 작고 하찮게 느꼈다는 문맥.
❌ ④ ahead(앞서): 산악에서 뒤처졌다는 문맥.
det.tip: passionate(열정적인) ↔ indifferent(무관심한), insignificant(하찮은) ↔ important(중요한).

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's (A)[encouragement / criticism], I participated eagerly in all the training courses. As a domestique, I was riding in front of Gabriel to (B)[shield / expose] him from the headwind. Everything was going perfectly until I crashed due to a crack in the road. Gabriel's injury was more serious. He (C)[urged / forbade] me to continue on his behalf.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Gabriel의 격려(encouragement)에 힘입어. 맞바람으로부터 보호하기(shield) 위해. 계속 가라고 재촉했다(urged).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ encouragement — shield — urged: 원문 일치.
❌ ① criticism(비판): encouragement의 반의어.
❌ ② expose(노출시키다): shield의 반의어.
❌ ③ forbade(금지하다): urged의 반의어.
det.tip: encouragement(격려) ↔ criticism(비판), shield(보호하다) ↔ expose(노출시키다), urged(재촉하다) ↔ forbade(금지하다).

questions.passage: Before the race started, I looked around the crowd, and I couldn't believe my eyes! My hero, Gabriel Martinez, the cycling world champion, was standing there! I ran over and asked, "You're Gabriel Martinez, right? Can I have your ①<u>autograph</u>?" He smiled and said, "If you win, you can." Excited by what he said, I pedaled harder than ever. I came in first and Gabriel was ②<u>waiting</u> at the finish line. As promised, he handed me his autograph saying, "You ③<u>outran</u> the others by two laps! You're a real ④<u>beginner</u>, kid!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ beginner(초보자) → racer(선수): 두 바퀴나 앞섰으므로 '진정한 선수'라고 칭찬한 것.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ beginner → racer: 2바퀴 앞서 우승한 아이를 '초보자'라 부르는 것은 모순.
❌ ① autograph(사인): 영웅에게 사인을 달라고 하는 맥락.
❌ ② waiting(기다리고 있는): 결승선에서 기다렸으므로 적절.
❌ ③ outran(앞섰다): 2바퀴 앞서 우승했으므로 적절.
det.tip: racer(선수) ↔ beginner(초보자). outrun = ~보다 앞서 달리다.

questions.passage: For several years, I assisted Gabriel in races as a domestique. As we cycled together, our team's results ①<u>flourished</u>. When the time came for his retirement, Gabriel asked the members if I could lead the team in his final race. He said he could no longer ride faster than me in the last sprint to the finish line and ②<u>insisted</u> that I ought to be the team leader. I was deeply ③<u>touched</u> and felt a ④<u>relief</u> on my shoulders. I was determined to make him proud.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① relief(안도감) → burden(부담): 팀 리더 역할은 '안도'가 아니라 '부담'을 느끼게 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ touched(감동받은): 깊이 감동했으므로 적절.
❌ ① flourished(번성하다): 성과가 좋아졌으므로 적절.
❌ ② insisted(주장하다): 팀 리더가 되어야 한다고 주장.
✅ ④ relief → burden: 감동하면서도 어깨에 '부담'을 느꼈다는 맥락.
det.tip: burden(부담) ↔ relief(안도). 'felt a burden on my shoulders' = 어깨에 부담을 느끼다.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These bumpy roads were a true test of ①<u>endurance</u>, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without ②<u>hesitation</u>, saying, "Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members ③<u>urged</u> me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our ④<u>comfort</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ comfort(편안함) → limits(극한): 극한까지 자신을 밀어붙이며 계속했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ comfort → limits: 'pushing ourselves to our limits' = 극한까지 밀어붙이다. comfort는 맥락과 모순.
❌ ① endurance(지구력): 250km 경주는 지구력의 시험.
❌ ② hesitation(망설임): 주저 없이 자전거를 내밈.
❌ ③ urged(재촉하다): 팀원들이 격려하며 재촉.
det.tip: limits(극한) ↔ comfort(편안함). 'push oneself to one's limits' = 극한까지 밀어붙이다.

questions.passage: Since then, Gabriel has been my mentor. When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and __________. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ insignificant(하찮은): 'felt small and ~'에서 small과 유사한 부정적 감정.
❌ ① confident(자신감 있는): small과 모순.
❌ ② proud(자랑스러운): small과 모순.
❌ ④ superior(우월한): small과 완전 반대.
det.tip: insignificant = unimportant = 하찮은. 'small and insignificant' = 작고 보잘것없는.

questions.passage: Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated eagerly in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones. Soon after, my efforts finally __________ in one of the mountain courses. As a domestique, I was riding in front of Gabriel to shield him from the headwind. Our team was far ahead of the others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② paid off(결실을 맺다): 열심히 훈련한 노력의 결과.
❌ ① fell apart(무너지다): 긍정적 결과와 모순.
❌ ③ gave up(포기하다): 결실과 반대.
❌ ④ broke down(고장나다): 노력이 고장난다는 것은 부자연스러움.
det.tip: pay off = 결실을 맺다, 보상을 받다. 'efforts paid off' = 노력이 보답하다.

questions.passage: They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel. However, when I looked over, I could see the pride in his eyes. He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not __________ me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears welled up in my eyes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① addressed(부르다/칭하다): 'address someone as ~' = ~라고 부르다.
❌ ② ignored(무시하다): 호칭과 무관.
❌ ③ punished(벌하다): 문맥 불일치.
❌ ④ replaced(교체하다): 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: address + 사람 + as ~ = ~라고 부르다/칭하다. 'addressed me as kid' = 나를 꼬마라고 불렀다.

questions.passage: Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix, a 250 km race famed for its cobblestone sections. These <u>bumpy</u> roads were a true test of endurance, talent, and mental power for every cyclist. As the race started, I focused on my strategy and my desire to win. However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 bumpy의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ rough(거친): bumpy와 동의어. 울퉁불퉁한 표면.
❌ ① smooth(매끄러운): bumpy의 반의어.
❌ ② wide(넓은): 도로 너비와 무관.
❌ ③ flat(평평한): bumpy의 반의어.
det.tip: bumpy = rough = uneven (울퉁불퉁한) ↔ smooth = flat (매끄러운, 평평한).

questions.passage: I was deeply touched and felt a burden on my shoulders. I was <u>determined</u> to make him proud. Gabriel's final race was the Paris-Roubaix.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 determined의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② resolved(결심한): determined과 동의어.
❌ ① hesitant(망설이는): determined의 반의어.
❌ ③ uncertain(불확실한): determined의 반의어.
❌ ④ reluctant(꺼리는): determined의 반의어.
det.tip: determined = resolved = decided (결심한, 단호한) ↔ hesitant = reluctant (망설이는).

questions.passage: The crowd roared <u>tremendously</u>. They focused on me since I was the first to cross the finish line. As I stood on the podium holding the trophy high, I felt like the glory should go to Gabriel.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 tremendously의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ enormously(엄청나게): tremendously와 동의어.
❌ ① quietly(조용히): tremendously의 반의어.
❌ ② slightly(약간): tremendously의 반의어.
❌ ④ gently(부드럽게): 환호와 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: tremendously = enormously = immensely = hugely (엄청나게).

questions.passage: When I turned nineteen, he brought me into his professional team, where only the most skilled and passionate cyclists came together. I felt small and <u>insignificant</u>. I could sprint the fastest on flat courses, but I always fell behind in mountain races. The Netherlands is mostly flat, so I had rarely cycled up steep slopes before.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 insignificant의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① significant(중요한): insignificant의 반의어.
❌ ② trivial(사소한): insignificant와 동의어.
❌ ③ minor(작은): insignificant와 유사어.
❌ ④ negligible(무시할 만한): insignificant와 동의어.
det.tip: insignificant = trivial = minor ↔ significant = important = major.

questions.passage: However, the rocky and cobblestone track caused a flat tire and I could not continue. Gabriel offered me his bike without <u>hesitation</u>, saying, "I remember your finishing the race two laps ahead of everyone when I first met you. Never stop pedaling, kid. I'll catch up." The rest of the members urged me on and we continued, pushing ourselves to our limits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 hesitation의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ confidence(확신): hesitation의 반의어. 주저 없이 행동.
❌ ① doubt(의심): hesitation과 유사어.
❌ ② reluctance(꺼림): hesitation과 유사어.
❌ ③ uncertainty(불확실): hesitation과 유사어.
det.tip: hesitation = doubt = reluctance ↔ confidence = certainty = decisiveness.

questions.passage:
(A) I entered the race as the youngest rider. Before the <u>race</u> started, I looked around the crowd.

(B) People of every <u>race</u> and background came together to celebrate the festival.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 race의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 경주 — 인종: (A)는 자전거 대회 맥락, (B)는 다양한 사람들 맥락.
❌ ② 의미 뒤바뀜.
❌ ③ (B)도 '경주'가 아닌 '인종'.
❌ ④ (A)도 '인종'이 아닌 '경주'.
det.tip: race 다의어: ① 경주(competition) ② 인종(ethnic group).

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who gives advice and support to a less experienced person over a period of time"

det.korean: 오랜 기간 경험이 적은 사람에게 조언과 도움을 주는 사람 = 멘토(mentor).
det.analysis:
✅ ② mentor(멘토): 조언과 도움을 제공하는 경험 있는 사람.
❌ ① rival(경쟁자): 도움이 아닌 경쟁.
❌ ③ competitor(경쟁자): rival과 동의어.
❌ ④ spectator(관중): 조언이 아닌 관람.
det.tip: mentor = 멘토/조언자. 본문에서 Gabriel이 Bliksem의 mentor.

questions.passage: Gabriel would say, "Riding uphill is painful, but the view at the top is fantastic." Motivated by Gabriel's encouragement, I participated __________ (eager) in all the training courses, especially the uphill ones.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis: participated(동사)를 수식하는 부사가 필요. eager(adj.) → eagerly(adv.).
det.tip: eager(형용사: 열망하는) → eagerly(부사: 열렬히). 동사 수식 → 부사.

questions.passage: Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. I'm so proud of you!" He said, "That trophy is yours, Captain." It was the first time he had not addressed me as "kid." My teammates approached me as tears __________ (well) up in my eyes.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.analysis: 과거시제 문맥 (approached). well(v. 솟구치다) → welled(과거형).
det.tip: well up = (눈물이) 솟구치다. well-welled-welled. 'tears welled up in my eyes' = 눈에 눈물이 고이다.

questions.passage: Pedaling with all my strength, I finished second in that race, but I felt a sense of guilt for my fellow team members. I should have been more careful. If I had not crashed, Gabriel would have come in first place, and our team would have won. Surprisingly, Gabriel gave me a gentle hug and said, "I knew you could do it. __________!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Gabriel이 가볍게 안아 주며 "네가 정말 자랑스러워(I'm so proud of you)!"라고 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ I'm so proud of you: Surprisingly(놀랍게도) + gentle hug 맥락. 죄책감 느끼는 주인공에게 자랑스럽다고 격려.
❌ ① disappointed(실망한): gentle hug와 모순.
❌ ② tried harder(더 노력했어야): 안아주며 비난하지 않음.
❌ ④ need more practice(더 연습 필요): 격려가 아닌 질책.
det.tip: Surprisingly = 예상 밖. 주인공은 죄책감을 느꼈지만 Gabriel은 오히려 자랑스러워함.

questions.passage: He cut in front of me and said, "Save your energy now for the final sprint. We'll help you to the finish line." Our speed increased as we approached the finish line, and my teammates worked hard to support me. When the finish line came into view, I began my final sprint with a rush of adrenaline, and our rivals were right on my tail, fighting for the same victory. Finally, I crossed the finish line ahead of my competitors __________. The crowd roared tremendously.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경쟁자들을 아주 근소한 차이로(by a nose) 앞서 결승선을 통과했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ by a nose(근소한 차이로): rivals were right on my tail(바로 뒤를 쫓음) → 근소한 차이 승리.
❌ ① by miles(큰 차이로): '바로 뒤를 쫓았다'와 모순.
❌ ② with ease(쉽게): rivals가 바로 뒤를 쫓았으므로 쉽지 않았음.
❌ ③ after giving up(포기한 후): 포기하지 않고 질주했음.
det.tip: by a nose = 아슬아슬하게/근소한 차이로. 'right on my tail' = 바로 뒤를 쫓다.
